task_instance: Get the latest Bitcoin crypto news headlines from the past 4 hours, i.e. run the skill's aggregator as 'news_aggregator.py --coin BTC --period 4h' and present the ranked articles (source, title, age, relevance score) plus the feed-health summary.
blocker_detail: The skill's sole core deliverable is to execute a bundled Python program (the news_aggregator entry point, which imports feedparser/requests/pyyaml, fetches configured RSS feeds over the network, filters by coin/category/time window and ranks articles). The office-assistant runtime grants only reading/writing/editing text files and web fetch/search; it cannot run any code, shell command, or Python script and cannot install packages, so the aggregator cannot be executed to produce the ranked-news output. The bundled scripts are present (not missing), so writing a substitute or mocking the feed data is disallowed; the gap is code execution in the runtime.
evidence: Read SKILL.md at plugins/crypto/crypto-news-aggregator/skills/aggregating-crypto-news/SKILL.md: Instructions and Examples sections every step is 'python ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/news_aggregator.py ...'; allowed-tools declares Bash(python:*); Prerequisites require Python 3.8+ and 'pip install feedparser requests pyyaml' plus internet. Glob of the skill repo confirms the bundled scripts exist (scripts/news_aggregator.py, feed_fetcher.py, feed_parser.py, scorer.py, formatters.py) and config/sources.yaml, so the blocker is not missing skill files. Executing that program requires running code, which the runtime does not permit (no Bash/shell, no code execution, no package install); therefore the deliverable (a produced and verified ranked crypto-news table/JSON from live feeds) cannot be generated or verified. No files beyond this result.json were produced in the work directory.
